title: Do not return a local by reference
description:
`makeGreeting` builds a string in a local variable and returns a **reference** to it. The local is destroyed when the function returns, so the caller is left holding a reference to nothing. The compiler warns about exactly this.

Fix the function so that it hands the string back safely. Returning by value is cheap here: the string is moved out, not copied.
hints: Change the return type from `std::string&` (or `const std::string&`) to plain `std::string`. The body can stay the same; the result is now moved out to the caller.
rules: The compiler must report no warnings.
unitTests:
static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(makeGreeting("x")), std::string>, "makeGreeting should return std::string by value");
TEST("greets") { CHECK_EQ(makeGreeting("Ada"), "Hello, Ada!"); CHECK_EQ(makeGreeting("a rather long name that will not fit in a small buffer"), "Hello, a rather long name that will not fit in a small buffer!"); }

grading.unitTests:
